title: Onramp Arcade: 30-minute hands-on SDK playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, hands-on playbook to run a 30-minute interactive onboarding session ("Onramp Arcade") that helps an engineer take an app from zero to a validated SDK call with observability hooks and a failure-mode lab. Target audience: engineers who want a low-friction, production-aware first loop with Redwood SDKs (web, node, and mobile).

Why this flow: 
- Fast feedback: we optimize for observable wins in <30m (auth, sample request, streaming, telemetry).
- Failure-first: deliberately exercises network and quota failure paths so teams leave with runbooks, not just success screenshots.
- Telemetry-backed: standard events and traces are recorded so we can iterate on friction hotspots.

Session length and roles:
- 0–5m: intro + setup check (host + participant)
- 5–20m: code lab (sample app + first SDK call + streaming)
- 20–27m: fault-injection lab (lossy network, rate limit, fallback to smaller model)
- 27–30m: wrap-up, next steps, feedback capture

Prereqs (participant):
- Laptop with Node 18+ or Python 3.11, and Docker installed (optional for local mock)
- GitHub account (for cloning example)
- Access to Central feature-flag dashboard (if running with flags)
- API key (temporary dev token) — host will provide

Host prep checklist:
- Create temporary sandbox API key with moderate quotas (token cap 100k/day)
- Seed a minimal app repo under github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/onramp-arcade and ensure tests pass
- Short-lived confluence note with session id + telemetry tag (e.g., onramp-arcade-YYYYMMDD)
- Provision a dummy project in console with logging retention = 7 days

Quickstart steps (Node example):
1) Clone the repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples.git && cd sdk-examples/onramp-arcade
2) Install: npm install
3) Set env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-dev-arcade-XXXXXX
4) Start local dev server: npm run dev (port 3456)
5) Run sample request: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"Summarize: product spec v1"}' http://localhost:3456/api/generate | jq -r .text

Expected successful output: a 1–3 sentence summary. If you see 401/403 — check API key or org binding; if 429 — check sandbox quota and host-provided capacity.

Streaming demo (2–3 min):
- Switch sample to streaming mode (npm run dev -- --stream) and open the browser playground endpoint /stream-playground
- Observe incremental tokens in the browser console and console trace in the console (trace id prints as TRACE:<id>)

Telemetry and traces to inspect (post-run):
- Event names (string): ["sdk.init", "sdk.request.start", "sdk.request.chunk", "sdk.request.end", "sdk.fallback.trigger", "sdk.error"]
- Minimum telemetry properties: sdk_version, runtime (node/browser), latency_ms, model, route, trace_id
- Where to look: Console -> Traces -> filter trace_id from the sample run; Logs -> search tag onramp-arcade-YYYYMMDD

Fault-injection lab (core of resilience learning):
A) Network loss (simulate via Chrome devtools throttle or tc in Docker):
- Expected behavior: request still completes within user-app timeout using prefix KV cache where possible, or triggers client-side retry.
- Failure-mode check: confirm sdk.request.start then either several sdk.request.chunk events or a sdk.error with code NETWORK_TIMEOUT.

B) Rate limit simulated (force 429):
- How: temporarily lower sandbox quota or use a gateway toggle (host toggles project.qps=0.1)
- Expected behavior: SDK automatically falls back to a smaller model variant (gpt-micro) or returns a structured error with suggestions.
- Checkpoints: Observe sdk.fallback.trigger event with property fallback_to=gpt-micro

C) Model quality regression (soft-failure):
- Switch dev model to a trimmed quantized variant and run the standard prompt suite. Compare scores printed in the local test harness (BLEU-ish heuristics).
- Expected action: mark as a quality regression in the console and file a quick bug in JIRA with telemetry link.

Developer narrative cookbook (mini-guides you can copy-paste):
- If you see lots of 429s during the lab: "Numbers first" — capture request rate (console sample: requests_per_minute), current model, avg latency. Then escalate to Dedicated trial or enable caching suggestions via Redwood Optimize.
- If streaming stalls in the browser: ask participant to open devtools -> network -> ws frames; confirm server sent chunked payloads. If server sent but browser didn't render, blame: client-render loop.

Quick runbook snippets (copyable):
- Revoke and reissue dev key: redwood-cli auth revoke --key sk-dev-arcade-XXXX && redwood-cli auth create --name "onramp-arcade-temp" --scopes generate,stream
- Force fallback to smaller model (developer only): export REDWOOD_PREFERRED_MODEL=gpt-micro && npm restart

Signal collection & feedback:
- At wrap, ask 3 quick metrics: "Could you run the sample in under 10 minutes?" "Did you understand the fallback behavior?" "What broke and how long did you wait before asking for help?" Capture answers in a short Google Form linked under linked_artifacts.

Open questions TODOs for the playbook:
- Should we add a pre-seeded Postgres cache example for stateful SDK usage? (pros: realistic; cons: longer setup).
- Can we automate provisioning of a disposable sandbox per session (one-click)? POC ticket: JIRA-DEVPATH-489.
- Consider a mobile-first variant that uses lower-bandwidth sampling and local on-device caching—need mobile engineer signoff.

Known rough edges (notes from prior runs):
- Windows users need WSL for the "tc" network tooling; provide an alternate Docker route.
- Some corporate proxies rewrite TLS SNI and block streaming TCP — fallback path should be highlighted early.
- Developers sometimes confuse streaming vs chunked polling; clarify difference in the intro slide.

Quick checklist to ship this playbook as a public micro-product:
- [ ] Create one-click sandbox provisioning flow
- [ ] Add automated telemetry tags per session
- [ ] Author a mobile-labs variant (iOS + Android)
- [ ] Curate 3 small prompt sets for quality checks (doc, code, conversation)
- [ ] Bake playbook into the SDK repo README with a single script: ./onramp-arcade.sh

Appendix: tiny troubleshooting matrix
- 401/403: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, check org binding, review policy in Console -> API keys
- 429: capture trace_id, switch to fallback model, file a ticket if persistent
- 502/504 (gateway): retry with exponential backoff; if persistent >5min, check region reachability and open SRE channel
- Streaming hang: check websocket frames, server traces; if server shows chunk emissions but client doesn't render, check frontend loop

Notes to self (host): leave sticky points and circle back on playbook after 3 runs. Collect anonymized telemetry and reword the troubleshooting matrix with real failure frequencies.

End of doc.
